newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says prospects for peace not good.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says prospects for peace not good.

text.p: Egypt on Saturday said it was not optimistic about the Middle East peace process because Israel had not progressed in implementing agreements hammered out with the Palestinians.
Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters that if Israel did not make good on its promises, the credibility of the negotiating process would be at stake.
He was speaking after Palestinian President Yasser Arafat briefed Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on the first meeting between Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"The picture does not look good in the absence of implementation," Moussa said. "Until now we see no progress."
He said the meeting on Wednesday between the Palestinian and Israeli leaders was important, but that implementation of agreements was crucial.

"All those agreements will have to be respected in full otherwise the credibility of agreements and the credibility of the peace itself will be at stake. Under such conditions there will be question marks about the derivatives of the peace process, including meetings on a regional level," Moussa said.
Moussa was referring to a Middle East economic conference that his country is due to host in November.

The Egyptian ambassador to Israel said last week that Israel had three weeks to start implementing PLO-Israel peace deals or the conference, aimed at integrating the Jewish state with Arab markets, would be cancelled.
The Palestine Liberation Organisation and Israel in 1993 signed a peace deal paving the way for limited Palestinian self-rule in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank.
Netanyahu's rejection of the principle of trading Arab land for peace has jeopardised further talks between the two sides.
Moussa disagreed openly with Netanyahu earlier on Saturday over the possiblity of a Palestinian state, saying such a state was an essential ingredient in Middle East peace.
Netanyahu angered Palestinians and other Arabs by telling his hardline Likud bloc after the meeting with Arafat that he would never allow a Palestinian state alongside Israel.
In 1979 Egypt became the first Arab country to sign a peace treaty with Israel and has since mediated between the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours.
